question: Which riverine Doab pairing is incorrectly matched?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2 - Bisht Doab – Beas and Chenab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bari Doab:** It lies between the **Beas** and **Ravi rivers** in the Punjab region. This pairing is **correct**.
 
• **Bisht Doab:** Incorrectly paired as lying between **Beas** and **Chenab**. The Bisht Doab is actually between the **Beas** and **Sutlej rivers**. Hence, this pairing is **incorrect**.
 
• **Rachna Doab:** Located between the **Ravi** and **Chenab rivers**. This pairing is **correct**.
 
• **Jech Doab:** Lies between the **Chenab** and **Jhelum rivers**. This pairing is **correct**.
 
• The concept of Doabs is significant in the study of the geography of the **Indus River system**, particularly in India and Pakistan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Doab:**

 
 
• The term **Doab** is derived from Persian, where "Do" means two, and "Ab" means water or river, referring to a region between two rivers.
 
• Doabs are common in the **Indus River system**, which flows through India and Pakistan.
 
• These regions are highly fertile due to the availability of abundant **water resources** and alluvial soil.
 
 
 
• **Key Doabs in Punjab:**
 
 
• **Bari Doab:** Lies between the **Ravi** and **Beas**. This area is known for its rich agricultural yield and historical significance.
 
• **Bisht Doab:** Lies between the **Beas** and **Sutlej rivers**. Incorrectly paired in the question. It is also highly fertile.
 
• **Rachna Doab:** Lies between the **Ravi** and **Chenab**, forming an agriculturally important region.
 
• **Jech Doab:** Lies between the **Chenab** and **Jhelum**. Historically significant for the ancient city of Harappa.
 
 
 
• **Indus River System:**
 
 
• The Indus River system is one of the largest drainage systems in the world, flowing through India and Pakistan.
 
• Major rivers in this system include **Indus, Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej**.
 
• The system supports an extensive network of **agriculture** and is vital for irrigation in the Indian subcontinent.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Importance:**
 
 
• Doabs play a crucial role in defining the **agricultural landscapes** and water management systems in the region.
 
• They are often considered as the lifelines for farming communities due to their **water availability** and fertile soil.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Significance:**

 
 
• Doabs in the Indus River system have been centers for ancient civilizations like the **Harappan Civilization**.
 
• They were historically important for trade, agriculture, and settlement due to their natural resources.
 
 
 
• **Modern Usage:**
 
 
• These regions continue to be vital for **irrigation projects** and serve as the agricultural backbone for India and Pakistan.
 
• Several canals and water management systems are built in these areas to optimize usage.
